title: What Happens When You Hit Enter

sections.name: Hook
lines: type
You type a web address and hit Enter.
timer
Less than a second later, the page is on your screen.
title
But in that second, your request crosses a city, maybe an ocean, and back. Here is every step.

sections.name: Finding the address
lines: names
Step one. Computers don't understand names like example dot com. They only understand numbers, called IP addresses.
cache
So your browser checks its memory first. If you visited recently, it already knows the number.
dns
If not, it asks a DNS server, the phone book of the internet. That server asks the root servers, then the dot com servers, then the website's own server.
ip
And an answer comes back. A number, like this one.

sections.name: The journey
lines: packets
Step two. Your request is chopped into small pieces called packets. Each one is labelled with where it came from and where it's going.
routes
Routers pass them along, hop by hop. Packets from the same message can even take different paths, and get put back in order at the end.
cable
Across oceans, they travel as pulses of light through cables on the sea floor, at about two hundred thousand kilometres per second.

sections.name: The handshake
lines: shake
Step three. Before sharing anything, your device and the server shake hands. Hello. Hello, I hear you. Great, let's talk.
lock
Then they agree on secret keys, so anyone who intercepts the packets sees only scrambled noise. That's the padlock next to the address.

sections.name: The server answers
lines: server
Step four. The server reads your request, finds the page, and sends back a response. Status two hundred. OK.
html
What arrives first is HTML, a text file describing the page.
fanout
Inside it are links to more files. Styles, scripts, images. So your browser fires off dozens more requests, many at the same time.

sections.name: Drawing the page
lines: render
Step five. The browser builds a tree of every element, applies the styles, works out where each box goes, and paints the pixels.
done
And the page appears. All of it, usually in well under a second.

sections.name: Recap
lines: recap
Find the address. Send the packets. Shake hands. Get the files. Draw the page.
outro
You do this dozens of times a day, without thinking about it. Follow for more of the tech you use every day.
